sources: Codex's hooks documentation, developers.openai.com/codex/hooks (redirecting to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks), read 2026-11-10; the page states no version or date, so its list is taken as Codex CLI 0.167.0's only where the binary agrees

the event names Codex CLI 0.167.0's own binary knows, read on the far-side pass of 2026-11-09 (a dump hook registered on every name; Codex ignores a name it does not know without a word); the documentation names the same fourteen
live runs of Codex CLI 0.167.0 recorded in 0.167.0/ (2026-11-09)
provenance: Event names come from Codex's hooks documentation, its binary and the recordings; `when`, `disposition` and `lost` are treecontext's own words. Nothing mechanical sees an event Codex has that neither this list nor a recording names, so the hooks documentation is re-read at every Codex upgrade.

events.when: a session starts, resumes or compacts (the documentation also names clear and fork)
a tool call produced a result, a shell command's non-zero exit and a write the sandbox refused included
the developer interrupts a turn of the main thread; no Stop fires for that turn
Codex is about to ask the developer to approve a call
events.lost: the approval prompt itself; whether a call the developer denies fires a PostToolUse is unrecorded, so such a call may leave only its PreToolUse account (a call Codex reported no result for)
the moment of each model request; no conversation content
each model request's status, error and token counts; no conversation content
the end of a compaction; Codex's payload carries no summary of the compacted conversation, so nothing the journal lacks. The SessionStart that follows it (source compact) is what the journal acts on
a session's end moment; declined until 0.1.0-beta.5, as for Claude Code (features/OUT-OF-SCOPE.md, D395)

events.when: Claude Code's event for a call that failed; Codex CLI 0.167.0 has no such event
events.lost: Codex states no outcome for a call: a shell command that exits non-zero arrives by PostToolUse with no exit code and is classed by its text, and a call of any other tool that fails (an MCP tool's error reply, a patch that did not apply) fires no PostToolUse, so it is journaled at its turn's end from its PreToolUse as a call Codex reported no result for, with no output and no class

events.when: Claude Code's account of every call of one assistant message; Codex CLI 0.167.0 has no such event
events.lost: an account of the calls the client resolved without running them; on Codex such a call is known only by its PreToolUse, journaled at its turn's end as a call Codex reported no result for, and a call that fired no PreToolUse at all leaves no entry
